draft.title: count_words: ASCII delimiter test fails — underscores, digits and non-ASCII letters retained in tokens
draft.body:
Synthetic token-counting consumer (local synthetic dependency `synthetic_tokens.py`; no external upstream or submission endpoint).

Specification: the command reads UTF-8 stdin and writes lowercase ASCII words and counts as tab-separated lines, sorted by word. A word is a maximal `[A-Za-z]+` match. Digits, underscores and all other characters delimit words. Empty input produces no output and exits successfully. Run `python3 count_words.py`; verify with `python3 -m unittest -v`.

Fixture commit: 0e5f7a0842d922209fe88dd0454c65a76fb6172e

Observed via runner-supplied reproduction (reported in the intake request; not independently host-observed by this governor): `python3 -m unittest -v` exits 1; stdout empty; test_ascii_delimiters FAILs, test_cli/test_count_sort_and_case/test_empty pass.

stderr excerpt:
```
FAIL: test_ascii_delimiters (test_count_words.CountingTest.test_ascii_delimiters)
  File ".../consumer/test_count_words.py", line 15, in test_ascii_delimiters
    self.assertEqual(counts("a_b 12 café"), [("a", 1), ("b", 1), ("caf", 1)])
AssertionError: Lists differ: [('12', 1), ('a_b', 1), ('café', 1)] != [('a', 1), ('b', 1), ('caf', 1)]
Ran 4 tests in 0.023s
FAILED (failures=1)
```

Cause unknown. Candidate areas (not yet evidenced): token selection (regex/word class in synthetic_tokens.py or consumer), normalization (case/Unicode handling), aggregation (counting/sorting).

Defect.observed: counts("a_b 12 café") returns [('12', 1), ('a_b', 1), ('café', 1)]: digits and underscores are kept inside/as tokens and the non-ASCII letter é is retained. `python3 -m unittest -v` exits 1 with test_ascii_delimiters FAIL (3 other tests pass), stdout empty.
Defect.expected: Per specification, words are maximal [A-Za-z]+ matches, lowercased; digits, underscores and all other characters delimit words. counts("a_b 12 café") == [('a', 1), ('b', 1), ('caf', 1)] and `python3 -m unittest -v` exits 0.
Defect.reproduction: At fixture commit 0e5f7a0842d922209fe88dd0454c65a76fb6172e, in the consumer directory run: `python3 -m unittest -v`. Observed exit 1, empty stdout, stderr reports FAIL test_ascii_delimiters at test_count_words.py line 15: `self.assertEqual(counts("a_b 12 café"), [("a", 1), ("b", 1), ("caf", 1)])` -> AssertionError: Lists differ: [('12', 1), ('a_b', 1), ('café', 1)] != [('a', 1), ('b', 1), ('caf', 1)]. Ran 4 tests; FAILED (failures=1).

members.summary: Source inspection identifies the `\w+` expression in the local synthetic dependency as the likely cause of the ASCII delimiter failure.

evidence.description: The specification defines words as maximal [A-Za-z]+ matches. The delimiter test expects counts("a_b 12 café") to return [('a', 1), ('b', 1), ('caf', 1)].

The tokenization boundary is the likely cause: tokens() uses re.findall(r"\w+", text). Python's Unicode word class includes digits, underscores, and letters such as é, while counts() only lowercases, counts, and sorts the returned tokens. This explains the reported output without requiring an aggregation defect.

uncertainties: The explorer could not execute commands, so the reported test failure and predicted direct token output were not independently observed.
The source inspection does not establish whether any additional inputs expose separate defects.

Run `python3 -c 'from synthetic_tokens import tokens; from count_words import counts; print(tokens("a_b 12 café")); print(counts("a_b 12 café"))'` to distinguish token selection from counting.
